modules.name: Radix sort

topic_descriptor.k: radixsort - pseudocode

modules.note: The attached manual supplies radix sort as pseudocode only. The trace uses decimal-symbol input, so R = 10; it does not present generated C. Supplemental extension, written by the tracer and not part of the manual (CAP-051): the quoted pseudocode assumes every key already has the same m symbols and supplies no step that establishes it. Rather than refuse ordinary unequal-width input, this module pads each shorter key on the left, the most-significant end, with the symbol 0, up to the longest key's width m. A leading 0 does not change what a decimal numeral denotes, and equal-width unsigned numerals compare lexicographically exactly as they compare numerically, so the padded keys sort into the same order as the ones entered; padding on the right would multiply each key by a power of R and misalign its units digit with the pass index i, which runs from m down to 1. Keys that already share a width are traced exactly as the manual states them, with no normalisation step at all.
